'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Israel–Hamas war]]
**[[2023 Israeli blockade of the Gaza Strip]]
***A [[fuel truck]] enters the [[Gaza Strip]] through the [[Rafah Border Crossing]] from [[Egypt]] for the first time since the war began. [https://www.manilatimes.net/2023/11/16/world/americas-emea/first-fuel-truck-enters-gaza-from-egypt-media/1920001 (AFP via ''The Manila Times'')]
**[[Siege of Gaza City]]
***[[Al-Shifa Hospital siege]]
****The [[Israel Defense Forces]] enter the [[Al-Shifa Hospital]] complex in [[Gaza City]] with [[infantry]] and tanks. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/live/world-middle-east-67400490 (BBC News)]
*[[Myanmar civil war (2021–present)|Myanmar civil war]]
**[[Operation 1027]]
***The pro-democracy [[National Unity Government of Myanmar|National Unity Government]] says that over 200 [[Myanmar Army|junta troops]] and their families have surrendered to rebel forces near [[China–Myanmar border|the border]] with [[China]]. [https://www3.nhk.or.jp/nhkworld/en/news/20231115_38/ (NHK World)]
***The [[State Administration Council|military junta]] imposes a [[curfew]] in [[Sittwe]], the capital of [[Rakhine State]], with tanks reported on the city's streets. The [[Arakan Army]] reportedly captures dozens of policemen and soldiers. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/myanmar-rebels-says-dozens-junta-forces-surrender-captured-2023-11-15/ (Reuters)]
***The [[Myanmar National Democratic Alliance Army]] claims that an entire battalion of the [[Tatmadaw|military]] surrendered to the [[Three Brotherhood Alliance]] in [[Shan State]].  [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/world/entire-army-battalion-surrendered-myanmar-rcna125275 (NBC News)]
***Junta spokesperson [[Zaw Min Tun (general)|Zaw Min Tun]] accuses rebel groups of "destroying the whole country" and says that reports of captured [[military base]]s are "propaganda". [https://www.tbsnews.net/world/myanmar-rebels-says-dozens-junta-forces-surrender-captured-739838 (''The Business Standard'')]
**[[Operation 1107]]
***[[Karen people|Karenni]] rebels in [[Kayah State]] capture [[Loikaw University]], evacuating 170 members of the university staff and their families, as fighting continues in the city. [https://www.irrawaddy.com/news/war-against-the-junta/kayah-resistance-seizes-myanmar-junta-bases-in-state-capital.html (''The Irrawaddy'')]
*[[Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[Southern Ukraine campaign]]
***A [[Russian Armed Forces|Russian]] [[missile]] strike kills two [[emergency service|emergency workers]] and injures seven others in [[Zaporizhzhia Oblast]], [[Ukraine]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/one-killed-seven-injured-russian-strikes-zaporizhzhia-region-governor-2023-11-15/ (Reuters)]
*[[Sudanese civil war (2023–present)|Sudanese civil war]]
**[[Battle of Khartoum (2023–2025)|Battle of Khartoum]]
***Fighting continues in [[Jabal Awliya]], south of [[Khartoum]], with local sources claiming that the [[Rapid Support Forces]] took control of the Al Najumi air base and a road connecting the city to [[White Nile State]]. [https://sudantribune.net/article279399/ (''Sudan Tribune'')]
**Violence between rival tribes in [[South Darfur]] kills at least 30 people over three days of clashes. [https://www.dabangasudan.org/en/all-news/article/escalating-violence-in-south-darfur-sudan-chad-border-closed-by-rsf (Radio Dabanga)]

'''Disasters and incidents'''
*[[2023 Doda bus accident]]
**A bus carrying passengers slides off the road and falls down a 300-foot valley in [[Doda district]], [[Jammu and Kashmir (union territory)|Jammu and Kashmir]], [[India]], killing at least 39 people and injuring 19 others. [https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/jammu/many-feared-dead-after-bus-falls-into-gorge-in-jammu-and-kashmirs-doda-district/articleshow/105229774.cms (''TOI'')]

'''International relations'''
*[[APEC United States 2023]]
**[[China–United States relations]]
***[[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Joe Biden]] and [[Paramount leader|Chinese leader]] [[Xi Jinping]] hold talks in [[San Francisco]], [[California]], [[United States]], their first meeting in over a year. The talks are described as being positive with "real progress" being made on key issues such as [[illegal drug trade|drug trafficking]] and [[artificial intelligence]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/biden-xi-meet-us-china-military-economic-tensions-grind-2023-11-15/ (Reuters)]
*[[France–Syria relations]]
**[[France]] issues [[arrest warrant]]s for [[President of Syria|Syrian president]] [[Bashar al-Assad]] and his brother [[Maher al-Assad]] on charges of [[crimes against humanity]] and complicity in [[Human rights violations during the Syrian civil war|war crime]]s, including the 2013 [[Ghouta chemical attack]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/france-issues-arrest-warrants-against-syrias-president-assad-source-2023-11-15/ (Reuters)]
*[[Guyana–Venezuela relations]]
**[[Venezuela]] announces that it will proceed with a [[2023 Venezuelan referendum|referendum]] on the status of [[Guayana Esequiba]], despite [[Guyana]]'s petition to stop the referendum from being held. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/venezuela-tells-world-court-referendum-go-ahead-despite-guyana-resistance-2023-11-15/ (Reuters)]
*[[International reactions to the Israel–Hamas war]]
**[[United Nations Security Council Resolution 2712]]
***The [[United Nations Security Council|UN Security Council]] passes a resolution calling for humanitarian pauses in the conflict, the establishment of humanitarian corridors, and for the unconditional release of hostages taken by [[Hamas]]. [[Russia]], the [[United Kingdom]], and the [[United States]] abstained. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2023/11/15/unsc-adopts-resolution-calling-for-extended-humanitarian-pauses (Al Jazeera)]

'''Law and crime'''
*The [[Supreme Court of the United Kingdom]] rules that the British government's [[Rwanda asylum plan]], where [[illegal immigrants]] would be relocated to [[Rwanda]] for processing and resettlement, is unlawful. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-67423745 (BBC News)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2024 Bangladeshi general election]]
**The [[Bangladesh Election Commission]] announces that parliamentary elections will occur on January 7 next year, following weeks of violent protests by supporters of the opposition. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2023/11/15/bangladesh-set-to-hold-parliamentary-elections-on-january-7 (Al Jazeera)]
*[[President of Malawi|Malawian President]] [[Lazarus Chakwera]] suspends all publicly funded international travel for [[Government of Malawi|government]] officials, including himself, until the end of March, as part of measures to address the [[Malawi|country]]'s [[Economy of Malawi|economic]] challenges. [https://www.thecitizen.co.tz/tanzania/news/africa/malawi-s-president-chakwera-bans-himself-and-his-cabinet-from-foreign-travel-4436536 (AFP via ''The Citizen'')]
